teams.heading: Manager Lionel Danford appeals for funds to save deaf sevens campaign
teams.body: The Fiji men’s and women’s deaf rugby sevens teams are facing a major financial hurdle ahead of the upcoming World Deaf Rugby Sevens Championship in Tokyo. Team manager Lionel Danford revealed a funding gap of up to $70,000 remains for daily expenses and camp preparations, despite valuable kit sponsorship from PacificAus Sports. Many of the squad's players are currently unemployed and must cover their own transport costs to Sigatoka. Despite these hardships, preparations continue, including a crucial scrimmage session scheduled against Osea Kolinisau’s national sevens side.

lead.why: The Fiji deaf rugby sevens teams are facing a critical funding shortage of up to $70,000 for their upcoming World Championship in Japan.

teams.heading: Joe Carpenter targets George Furbank Premiership duel for England squad recall
teams.body: Sale Sharks full-back Joe Carpenter is targeting Sunday’s Premiership clash with Harlequins to outshine George Furbank and force his way back into Steve Borthwick’s plans. The Sale man has not featured for England since earning his sole cap in 2025, but his form has surged following a full pre-season. Only Immanuel Feyi-Waboso has beaten more defenders in the opening rounds of the domestic season, and Carpenter believes back-to-back performances will "put me in the best position to hopefully get involved come November."

lead.why: It highlights a direct selection narrative between a high-performing challenger and the incumbent England full-back ahead of the November international window.

teams.heading: Toulon begin search for new director after Pierre Mignoni's abrupt exit
teams.body: Toulon are still without a director of rugby following Pierre Mignoni’s sudden resignation earlier this week. Mignoni departed the Top 14 giants after a series of frustrations, reportedly accusing his players of not “behaving like competitors.” While the club’s leadership prioritises a swift appointment to restore order, no definitive successor has emerged in today’s reports. The vacancy remains the primary focus in the French domestic landscape as the national side prepares for the upcoming November internationals.

lead.why: Develops the ongoing story of Pierre Mignoni's exit from Toulon as the club begins its search for a successor.

teams.heading: Eddie O’Sullivan warns Andy Farrell after Leinster’s international front-row scrum struggles
teams.body: Former head coach Eddie O’Sullivan has flagged South Africa’s "frightening" scrum dominance as a major concern for Andy Farrell ahead of the autumn internationals. Following Leinster’s recent 26-20 defeat to the Sharks, where a Test-strength front-row including Andrew Porter and Ronan Kelleher conceded eight scrum penalties, O’Sullivan suggested the Springboks’ physical power is becoming a problem for World Rugby. While acknowledging the challenge is not unique to Ireland, he noted that South Africa "take you to the woodshed" through sheer physical attrition.

lead.why: Former head coach Eddie O'Sullivan's warning about scrum dominance addresses a significant tactical concern for Ireland’s front-row ahead of the autumn Tests.

teams.heading: Italy face South Africa in Turin following previous home defeat
teams.body: Italy lost 32-14 to South Africa in the most recent meeting between the sides at home in November 2025. The Azzurri currently sit 11th in the Nations Championship log after three rounds of play. Gonzalo Quesada’s squad returns to home soil for the first time in the competition for this Round 4 fixture following a 57-10 defeat against Australia in Round 3. Italy have yet to record a victory in the tournament and currently carry a points difference of -94.

lead.why: The fixture marks Italy's return to Turin for a rematch of their 2025 meeting with the Springboks.

teams.heading: Scottish Rugby faces continued legal uncertainty over stalled concussion lawsuit
teams.body: The legal challenge regarding brain injuries in rugby union remains in a state of uncertainty as claimants navigate a multi-million-pound financial hurdle. Although former players won a significant court battle in August to prevent World Rugby and Scottish Rugby from having the case thrown out, the litigation is currently hindered by a £2.8 million bill for legal costs. This impasse must be resolved before the group, which includes several former internationals, can proceed with their pursuit of damages for neurological conditions.

teams.heading: Welsh Rugby Union publishes report justifying the 2028 West Wales professional cull
teams.body: The Welsh Rugby Union has released the 68-page Keystone report detailing the evidence used to decide that only one professional team will represent West Wales from 2028. With Cardiff and the Dragons already granted capital and east licences, the Ospreys and Scarlets must now compete for the remaining slot. Union bosses maintain that funding cannot support four professional sides beyond the 2027-28 season. A final decision on which of the two historic west-Wales clubs will be culled is expected in June 2027.

lead.why: The release of the Keystone report provides the official institutional evidence and data justification for the upcoming reduction of Wales' professional regions.

teams.heading: Felipe Contepomi recruits Shaun Edwards and Mario Ledesma to backroom team
teams.body: Argentina head coach Felipe Contepomi has bolstered his support staff ahead of the Nations Championship resumption by recruiting Shaun Edwards and Mario Ledesma. Edwards, the renowned defence guru who helped France to three Six Nations titles, joins through to the 2027 World Cup. He is joined by former Pumas head coach Ledesma, who returns as forwards coach after four years away. Contepomi noted the pair bring “enormous international experience” to the squad before next month’s test against Ireland in Dublin.

lead.why: The recruitment of a world-renowned defence coach and a former head coach represents a major strategic upgrade for the national coaching staff.

teams.heading: Australia look to break 23-year Eden Park hoodoo against All Blacks
teams.body: The Wallabies face the daunting task of ending a winless run at Eden Park that stretches back to 1986. While the venue remains a fortress where the All Blacks are unbeaten since 1994, coach Les Kiss has maintained consistency, making only one change to his starting side as Isaac Henry replaces the suspended Hunter Paisami. Reflecting on the challenge, Kiss noted: “It’s got its own sense of atmosphere, that really can envelope you and it can suffocate you if you’re not ready.”

lead.why: It is the primary narrative in the rugby press today regarding Australia's immediate objective at Eden Park.

teams.heading: Japan Rugby Football Union hosts online forum to discuss future values
teams.body: The Japan Rugby Football Union held an online forum this week to mark its centenary, shifting focus toward the long-term societal impact of the game. Rather than focusing on match results, the event explored how the sport’s core values—the spirit of 'No Side', respect for diversity, and 'One Team'—can be integrated into wider social development. Top executives and stakeholders reviewed the union's history while discussing the evolving role of rugby within the modern era.

lead.why: This is a fresh report on the JRFU centenary forum discussing the future of Japanese rugby values.

teams.heading: Dave Rennie prepares All Blacks for high-stakes Eden Park Bledisloe clash
teams.body: New Zealand faces a significant test today, looking to protect a 53-match unbeaten record at Eden Park while navigating a lengthy casualty list. With captain Ardie Savea, Richie Mo'unga and several other key starters ruled out, coach Dave Rennie has prioritised mental resilience to counter the pressure. “No one wants to be part of the first team for a long time to lose at Eden Park or to lose the Bledisloe,” Rennie admitted, urging his side to use the external scrutiny as fuel.

teams.heading: Aoife Wafer ruled out of Ireland's WXV tests against South Africa
teams.body: Ireland forward Aoife Wafer will not travel to South Africa for the upcoming WXV Global Series matches. The player has been ruled out of the fixtures scheduled for 24 and 31 October in Cape Town due to an injury sustained during training. Ireland head coach Scott Bemand has named a 30-player squad for the trip, which includes the return of Ruth Campbell following an ankle recovery, while Sam Monaghan remains unavailable for selection due to an Achilles injury.

lead.why: The news of Aoife Wafer being ruled out of the upcoming WXV Global Series tests is a significant development for the Springbok Women's upcoming schedule.
